title: Pocket heuristics — context wrangling (Samira Qureshi, Mar 2028)
content:
Quick summary:
This is a compact scratchpad collecting short heuristics and cheap experiments for handling long context in production LLMs. Goal: practical knobs that reduce per-token cost and tail latency while keeping quality within a narrow band for product features (chat history, doc assist, agent traces). Not a formal paper — more like a field manual.

Papers / posts skimmed this sprint (hotnotes):
- "Adaptive prefix attenuation" (blog, Mar 2028) — idea: gradually downweight prefix tokens in attention or probabilistically evict older KV frames to bound compute.
- "KV shard eviction for heterogenous workloads" (arXiv 2803.01234) — empirical: cheap LRU + size-aware eviction beats time-only policies when documents have heavy long-range dependencies.
- "Stitch-first retrieval" (company blog) — keep short stitch tokens + anchor paragraphs instead of full doc prefix.

High-level takeaways (practical):
- Workload matters: conversational assistants with short, frequent turns => aggressive trimming works; long-form drafting / code => prioritize retention.
- Small losses in early tokens (first 64) are cheaper to accept than quality drop in recent 256 tokens. Users care about recency.
- Two-tier cache helps: always-keep (last N tokens / last k messages) + best-effort (LRU KV for older context).
- Quantization + shorter kv-embeddings: trade memory for compute latency — useful when GPU memory pressure causes batching to collapse.

Micro-experiments to run (cheap, 1–3 days each):
1) Eviction-policy sweep (baseline: time-based 30k tokens)
   - policies: time-LRU hybrid, size-aware LRU, recency-only, recency+sparse-sampling
   - metrics: per-token generation latency P50/P95, token-cost, cue-preservation F1 on small eval set (10 prompts)
   - quick pass: 1000 requests synthetic + 200 real-chat replay

2) Prefix attenuation ablation
   - method: multiply prefix attention logits by scalar alpha(t) where t=age bucket (alpha in [0.2,1])
   - measure: coherence drop vs hallucination rate, latency impact negligible (kernel constant?)

3) Stitch-first vs full-prefix on docs
   - method: pick anchor sentences (top-k by tf-idf) + 3-line stitch vs full prefix truncated to same token budget
   - metric: reranker A/B (human judgement for 100 cases) + embedding-sim delta

Notes on instrumentation / dashboards needed:
- Token-level source tagging (user-message, retrieved-doc, system-prompt, stitch) so cost per-source is visible in Console.
- KV-eviction event logging (timestamp, policy, evicted_token_count, upstream_request_id) to correlate with regressions.
- Small synthetic eval harness: 200 replayed sessions with binary pass/fail per session (keeps CI cheap).

Quick heuristics to try in the next sprint (deployable as runtime flags):
- Default keep: last 4 messages + last 2560 tokens; then allow best-effort 6k older tokens under low load.
- If per-request latency > target, trim oldest chunk(s) in 1280-token steps until meets SLO (fast fallback).
- For customers on Dedicated with tail-SLOs: maintain a separate small pinned KV for last-8 messages to guarantee recency.
- Stitch policy: keep 3 anchors per doc; anchor selection = first paragraph + highest-sim paragraph to prompt embedding.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does attenuation of prefix attention actually alter factual hallucination patterns (not just coherence)? Need targeted hallucination probes.
- How does the combination of quantization + prefix trimming interact? Could quantize-then-trim be worse than trim-then-quantize?
- Operational: eviction spikes correlate with autoscaler scaling events? If so, we should avoid synchronous evictions that amplify load.

Notes-to-self (messy):
- Keep experiment harness minimal; prefer replay logs over synthetic; real traffic reveals distributional edges.
- Talk to infra: can we emit a lightweight eviction trace event at 1k QPS without adding CPU overhead? Possibly offload to tracing sampler.
- Ask product (Evelyn): which features must preserve whole doc context vs which can be stitchy? Prioritize quality windows per product.

Draft rollout plan for a conservative experiment (for Hosted API):
- Week 0: baseline collection (1 week of replay).
- Week 1: implement size-aware LRU + logging behind flag; run internally on 5% of traffic (canary) for 3 days.
- Week 2: human eval + metric check (P95 latency, quality probes). If regressions < threshold, expand to 20% for 2 days.
- Abort if quality probe delta > 6% or P95 increases > 10%

References / links (scratch):
- Adaptive prefix attenuation (blog): https://distill.pub/adaptive-prefix-2028
- KV shard eviction draft (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2803.01234
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/48
- Context Cost Playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Context+Cost+Playbook

TODO (short):
- [ ] Spin up 48-hour eviction sweep on cheap cluster (use small model sim).
- [ ] Add eviction-event tags to span logs (trace id mapping).
- [ ] Set up 100-sample human eval template for stitch-first experiments.

Random ideas worth saving:
- "soft-eviction": degrade token importance instead of hard removal (downweight embeddings in retrieval scoring).
- Customer QoS lanes: give some customers a pinned KV ring (no eviction) vs flexible KV for cost-sensitive customers.

End of pocket notes. Keep short and return to this after the sweep.
